Lessons.Title: More Multiples
ExplanationParagraphs: Goal: interpret multiples of 6, 8 and 10 in real situations, including solutions that are impossible, several exact solutions and surplus packages. The 2021 first-edition source student PDF has 3 pages.

Warm-up 10 min: use original banquet seating illustration, ten chairs per table; each student records an estimate that is too low, about right and too high, then explains it to a partner. Source image and estimates are teacher-reviewed; do not use a guessed replacement.

Activity 1 20 min: the source restricts students to ONE table type (6 or 8 seats) and no empty chairs. Jada18: 3 tables of6. Noah30: 5 tables of6. Combined48: 8 tables of6 OR6 tables of8. Including two teachers50: neither type exactly seats all. Explain each of four distinct original questions with drawings, arrays or multiples.

Activity 2 15 min: hotdogs packs10, buns packs8. Lin50: 5 packs hotdogs, exactly50 buns impossible, 7 packs=56 buns to cover50. Diego72: 8 packs hotdogs=80, 9 packs buns=72; consider justified alternatives if surplus is permitted. Equal purchased counts may be40 or80. Explain every original problem part.
Lesson synthesis 10 min: exact versus at least, remainders, multiple or no exact solution and common multiples. Teacher records reasoning.

Independent FIRST-PARTY Edulytics Cool-down 5 min (NOT publisher original): 48 guests can fill 8 tables of6 or6 tables of8; 50 guests cannot fill either size without empty seats. Require a written reason; teacher reviews. Numeric exact Practice is a separate subskill.

KeyConcepts.Title: Exact seating
KeyConcepts.Definition: A whole number of one table type with no empty chairs.

KeyConcepts.Title: Minimum package coverage
KeyConcepts.Definition: Whole packages to meet or exceed demand.

KeyConcepts.Title: Shared multiples
KeyConcepts.Definition: Numbers divisible by both pack sizes.
